messages:
ashley: hi all, starting my onboarding — I tried `kubectl get ns` but got "Error from server (Forbidden)". My kubeconfig looks like it has a dev context but not sure why I'm blocked.

devops-amy: welcome ashley! :wave: can you paste the output of `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config get-contexts --no-headers`?

ashley: current-context=redwood-dev-ashley, get-contexts shows: redwood-prod, redwood-staging, redwood-dev-ashley (current).

ryan: sounds like context is right. Forbidden usually RBAC. Run `kubectl auth can-i get namespaces --all-namespaces` and `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n eng-sandbox`.

ashley: `no` for both.

devops-amy: OK, two things: 1) confirm you completed the infra access request form (we use that to add you to the eng-newhires group), 2) if you need to share a config for help, don't paste raw creds. Use `kubectl config view --minify --flatten > /tmp/ashley-kube.yaml` then scrub any token/exec creds before pasting.

ashley: I did the general HR onboarding but not the infra one. Where is it?

ryan: infra form is at https://intranet.redwood/onboard/infra (choose "k8s access" and list the namespaces you need). Pick the "dev clusters" option. After submit, our access job will run and create a RoleBinding in the requested namespaces (~5-20m).

infra-bot: access-request queued for user=ashley namespaces=[eng-sandbox] (request id: ar-78421). Processing...

ashley: perfect, submitted. Also my kubeconfig has `exec` SSO; will that be a problem for the automation?

devops-amy: exec is fine. The automation grants group membership at the identity provider level or adds a ClusterRoleBinding for your ID. If anything fails you'll see a failure email with instructions.

ryan: pro tip: to avoid hitting prod accidentally, create a per-repo kubeconfig: `kubectl config view --minify --flatten > .kubeconfig` in the repo, then `export KUBECONFIG=$PWD/.kubeconfig:$HOME/.kube/config` or use direnv. Also `kubectx` is handy for switching.

ashley: thanks. How do I confirm permissions after the job runs?

devops-amy: run `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n eng-sandbox` and `kubectl get pods -n eng-sandbox --no-headers`. If `can-i` still says no, paste the output here and we'll escalate.

infra-bot: access-request ar-78421: applied RoleBinding -> namespace=eng-sandbox subject=group:eng-newhires role=view (duration=indefinite).

ashley: trying now: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n eng-sandbox` -> "yes". `kubectl get pods -n eng-sandbox` shows a few running pods. yay! :tada:

ryan: woo! one last thing: if you ever need to share debug info, prefer `kubectl -n X get pod Y -o yaml` but redact `status.conditions[*].lastProbeTime` etc, and never share your flattened kubeconfig with exec token included.

ashley: got it. Saved the infra link and the cheat commands. thanks everyone :rocket:
